findings.summary: The risk says the pause may come from a line paused earlier for another reason. That case is already caught at the top of the loop, so the new check only changes things for a pause that begins during the last attempt.
findings.evidence: drain.rs 1745-1752 checks Steps::paused at every job boundary, before each read or run. So a line paused before the last attempt began never reaches the 1812 exit. Fix: Narrow the risk to a pause that began during the item's last attempt, or drop it. No code change.

findings.summary: The brief lists display.rs as a deliverable, but the plan leaves it unchanged. The plan's reason is correct, but the verifier may expect a diff there.
findings.evidence: display::drain renders RepeatedFailure only when failed_item is Some. On the Paused path set_stop is never called (finish 2413), so neither the stop nor failed_item is set. Fix: In the change description, say that display.rs needs no edit and why, so the missing deliverable is a recorded decision, not an omission.

summary: I checked the plan against the snapshot code. Drain::attempts (drain.rs 1725-1816) checks Steps::paused only at the top of the loop, at a job boundary (1745-1752). It returns ItemEnd::Failed at `failures >= ATTEMPTS` (1812-1814) without checking again. Drain::finish then turns Failed into Stop::RepeatedFailure unconditionally (2379). So when an item's second failure pauses its line, nothing notices before the stop. That is where the fault starts. One check at that exit, reusing ItemEnd::Paused, fixes it there. finish already turns Paused into one pass_over line and sets no stop (2413). The not-landed path is covered too, because `passed` stays Some and skips the top-of-loop check. I traced the dependency test: drain::drain works one item at a time (one_at_a_time truncates each wave). After a ends Paused, the re-plan in drain_with (2832-2837) calls prepare, which holds back everything that depends on a paused id (2041-2064). pass_over_paused (2115-2123) skips items already tried, so a gets no second line while c gets its "depends on a, which is held back" line. The plan's expected log and assertions are consistent with the Stub as it is: read and reread name the retry job `a-retry` (186), Steps::paused is asked with the item id, and the existing pause_on_run pattern (206-212) shows the new field fits. Without the fix, both new tests would fail on the log, the stop and failed_item. The existing repeated-failure tests (1047, 1073) set no pause, so they keep the stop. The dependents list covers finish, display.rs, the help text in main.rs, the per-wave re-plan, and the other RepeatedFailure tests. The approach is not a heuristic: it reads the scope guard's own pause state at the point where the item gives up. There is no cause classification, and no config, schema or external service is involved. The plan fits one producer run. I have no blocker or major findings.
